claim: Over a 30-week test period, ResiCast's one-week-ahead forecasts of absolute gene concentration were off by roughly 18 percent on average.
evidence: ResiCast forecast next-week absolute concentrations with a MAPE of 18.4 percent over the 30 test weeks, ranging from 12.9 percent for sul1 to 27.6 percent for blaCTX-M.
label: supported

claim: The two video annotators' step totals agreed very closely, with an intraclass correlation above 0.99.
evidence: Two trained annotators independently marked every heel strike in the video using a frame-stepping tool, and disagreements larger than two steps per bout were resolved by a third annotator. Inter-rater agreement on bout totals was high, with an intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.994.
label: supported

claim: Closing schools for four weeks once weekly ILI hit 1 percent cut the modelled peak by about a third and pushed it back by more than three weeks.
evidence: The four-week closure at the 1 percent trigger produced the largest change, lowering the peak to 873 per 100,000, a reduction of 32 percent, and delaying it by 23 days.
label: supported

claim: The wrist device overestimated total sleep time by 19 minutes, with the overestimate largest among night-shift workers.
evidence: In the laboratory substudy, epoch-by-epoch agreement between the device and polysomnography was 88.6 percent, and the device overestimated total sleep time by a mean of 19 minutes.
label: partially_supported

claim: Site H3 had a median blaCTX-M relative abundance of minus 2.14 log10, driven by effluent from the hospital's intensive care unit.
evidence: Site H3, downstream of St Aldric Infirmary, stood out for blaCTX-M, with a median relative abundance of minus 2.14 log10 compared with a median of site medians of minus 3.43 across the network.
label: partially_supported

claim: The HARBOR-ABM synthetic population was validated against mobile phone location data.
evidence: The synthetic population of 412,600 agents was generated from the invented 2018 Harrowmere household census, matching household size, age structure and district of residence across 37 districts.
label: unsupported

claim: NIGHTSHIFT-RT participants received a payment for each reaction-time test they completed.
evidence: Reaction time was measured with BriefPVT-5, a five-minute tablet test presenting a visual stimulus at random intervals of 2 to 10 seconds. Workers completed it at the start and end of each scheduled shift, giving 3,840 scheduled tests.
label: unsupported

claim: In the StepTrace validation the Kinetra Loop had the longest battery life of the three devices.
evidence: Each participant wore the Pacewell Band 3, the Kinetra Loop and the Corvi Strap simultaneously on the non-dominant wrist, stacked in an order randomised per participant. All devices ran manufacturer firmware with default step-detection settings, and counts were read from the minute-level exports of each device.
label: unsupported

claim: In SEWERWATCH-12 duplicate splits, blaCTX-M was the most reproducible target.
evidence: Duplicate splits showed a median coefficient of variation of 14.6 percent across targets, with blaCTX-M the least reproducible at 21.3 percent because of its low concentrations.
label: contradicted

claim: In the HARBOR-ABM no-closure baseline, the cumulative attack rate was 32.4 percent.
evidence: In the baseline, weekly incidence peaked at 1,284 per 100,000 in week 9 and the cumulative attack rate was 27.4 percent, reaching 41.2 percent among children aged 5 to 14.
label: contradicted
